The forward problem is described by the time-harmonic Maxwell equations with a local inhomogeneity in the refractive index.
The inverse problem aims to reconstruct the refractive index perturbation from far-field measurements of the scattered electromagnetic field for multiple incident waves.
The inverse problem is formulated as a nonlinear, ill-conditioned system of equations F(x) = y, where x represents the coefficients of the refractive index perturbation.
The paper considers the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm and the iteratively regularized Gauss-Newton method (IRGNM) to solve the inverse problem.
Spectral preconditioning is used to efficiently solve the ill-conditioned linear systems that arise in the regularized Newton methods.
Lanczos' method is used to approximate the largest eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors of the Jacobian matrix for the spectral preconditioner.
The paper proposes an efficient implementation of a Lepski-type stopping rule to determine the optimal number of Newton iterations.
For the test example, the updated preconditioned IRGNM achieves an L2 error of 0.28 about 2.5 times faster than the Newton-CG method.
For data perturbed by random noise with a relative noise level of about 2%, the Lepski-type stopping rule outperforms the discrepancy principle.
The electric field is represented using between 98,304 and 786,432 degrees of freedom, and the refractive index perturbation is represented using 500 to 2000 coefficients.
The spectral preconditioning approach is particularly effective at approximating the isolated large eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix for exponentially ill-posed problems.
The efficient approximation of the propagated data noise error using the spectral decomposition of the preconditioned Jacobian avoids the need to solve multiple linear systems.
The updated preconditioned IRGNM recomputes and updates the spectral preconditioner during the Newton iterations, significantly reducing the number of inner iterations required.
The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed acceleration techniques for regularized Newton methods applied to the electromagnetic inverse medium scattering problem.

The numerical results show that the updated preconditioned IRGNM with the Lepski-type stopping rule outperforms other iterative regularization methods in terms of work-precision diagrams for both exact and noisy data.
